articles.title: Washington upgraded 7,474 low-income homes with weatherization, cutting energy costs by $1.4 million and supporting about 180 jobs
articles.summary: US News: Washington’s low-income weatherisation programme upgraded 7,474 households between July 2009 and June 2010, with the homes expected to receive about $.
articles.body: Washington’s low-income weatherisation programme upgraded 7,474 households between July 2009 and June 2010, with the homes expected to receive about $1.4 million in direct energy savings. According to a report by the Washington Policy Centre, the average weatherised household was estimated to save roughly $189 a year through lower energy costs. The programme also reported wider economic benefits, including around 180 jobs created or retained during the period. However, the 2011 report examined the programme’s costs alongside its claimed benefits, noting that an average project cost $6,070 and that energy savings alone did not exceed programme costs under the scenarios assessed.Washington households saved about $189 a yearThe Department of Commerce figures put the direct energy savings associated with the 7,474 weatherised homes at $1.4 million. This was presented as one of the main benefits of the programme, alongside the number of households that received improvements.The figures work out to roughly $187 in direct energy savings per weatherised household when the reported $1.4 million is divided across 7,474 homes. However, the report gives a more specific estimate of about $189 a year in direct energy savings for the average household, and that is the figure used in its discussion of household benefits.Weatherisation delivered annual economic benefitsCommerce estimated that the average weatherised household would receive nearly $385 in total annual economic benefit. Of that amount, less than half was attributed to direct energy savings, which the report puts at roughly $189 per year.The remaining $196 per year was attributed to non-energy benefits, including lower delinquent bills, improved comfort, higher home values and reduced emissions. The report also noted that Commerce acknowledged uncertainty around these indirect benefits because they are difficult to measure. It quoted the Commerce report as saying: “Because non-energy benefits are difficult to measure, there is some uncertainty in our estimates.”Washington weatherisation projects created 180 jobsThe weatherisation programme was not only intended to reduce household energy costs. During the recession, policymakers also presented weatherisation spending as a way to support employment. The Department of Commerce reported that approximately 180 jobs were created or retained as a direct result of the weatherisation projects during the programme's period.The Washington Policy Centre’s 2011 report, however, examined the programme critically and argued that its economic and energy benefits needed to be considered alongside its costs. It noted that the average weatherisation project cost $6,070 and quoted the Commerce report as stating: “Note that energy benefits alone do not exceed Program costs for any of the scenarios.” The 7,474 weatherised homes and their energy savings are part of a wider debate over the programme’s overall cost-effectiveness, rather than simply an account of household savings.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Iran rules out reopening Strait of Hormuz, returning to US talks until conditions met
articles.summary: Middle East News: Iran has ruled out reopening the Strait of Hormuz or returning to the previous framework of negotiations with the United States until Washington meets.
articles.body: Iran has ruled out reopening the Strait of Hormuz or returning to the previous framework of negotiations with the United States until Washington meets Tehran’s conditions, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said, as tensions between the two countries continue to escalate.According to Iran’s Tasnim news agency, Ghalibaf said Tehran had conveyed its demands to Washington through intermediaries and would not change its position until its conditions were met.“Until these conditions are met, the legitimate rights of the Iranian nation are recognised, and the Americans’ commitments are implemented, there will be no opening for a return to the previous conditions for negotiations or the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz,” he said.The remarks came a day after Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran had conveyed its conditions for ending the conflict to Washington through Qatar.“Our conditions are an end to the war on all fronts, the release of our frozen funds and an end to the naval blockade,” Rezaei told Al Jazeera.The Strait of Hormuz has become a key point of contention in the confrontation. Iran’s Armed Forces spokesman Brigadier General Abolfazl Shekarchi said the initiative in the strategic waterway remained with Iran’s armed forces, according to Iran’s Tasnim news agency. He also rejected US statements on maritime traffic through the strait as a psychological operation.Iran has also issued fresh warnings over possible US military action. The Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters said any renewed US attack would trigger attacks against American bases and interests across the region, according to Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency.“Should the United States make any mistake against the Islamic Republic of Iran, all its bases and interests in the region will be targeted in continuous, effective and painful attacks without any limitation or consideration,” the military command said.The Iranian command also warned regional countries against supporting any US military operation against Tehran, saying countries that assist Washington would be considered participants in the action, according to IRNA.Meanwhile, US central command said its forces had redirected 109 commercial vessels as part of efforts to enforce Washington’s naval blockade against Iran. CENTCOM said the vessels were redirected as of September 20 to ensure compliance with the blockade.The US military resumed enforcement of the naval blockade against maritime traffic entering and leaving Iranian ports on July 14, according to CENTCOM.US President Donald Trump has meanwhile warned Iran of consequences if Tehran refuses to change its position, while also indicating that he could be open to talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during the UN General Assembly in New York.The latest developments come as world leaders gather in New York for the UN General Assembly, with the US-Iran confrontation and wider West Asia tensions expected to remain major issues during the diplomatic gathering.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A couple found a rare Mickey Mantle photo inside a baseball book at a garage sale; it later sold for $20,740
articles.summary: US News: A couple browsing an oversized Topps baseball-card coffee-table book at a local garage sale made an unexpected discovery when they found a rare photog.
articles.body: A couple browsing an oversized Topps baseball-card coffee-table book at a local garage sale made an unexpected discovery when they found a rare photograph of a young Mickey Mantle tucked inside. The photograph, later authenticated by PSA/DNA as a Type 2 print, captured Mantle during spring training early in his rookie season and became the source image for his iconic 1951 Bowman rookie card. The couple also found an image of Joe DiMaggio inside the same book, according to Heritage Auctions, which later offered the Mantle photograph for sale. The photograph was sold on December 20, 2025, during Heritage's Winter Sports Catalogue Auction, fetching $20,740. Its value was not simply tied to Mantle's fame. Details in the photograph, including his No. 6 uniform and the bat belonging to teammate Joe Collins, help place the image at a specific point in the young player's career.The photograph captured Mantle as an untested rookieHeritage's description places the photograph at Arizona spring training, when Mantle was still an untested rookie. One clue is his rolled-up sleeve. The auction house notes that Mantle would later have enough standing to dictate tailoring changes to his uniform, but was not yet in that position at the time the photograph was taken. Another detail is the bat resting over Mantle's right shoulder. Heritage identifies it as a bat belonging to Yankees first baseman Joe Collins. The auction description says Mantle had not yet signed a deal with Hillerich & Bradsby for his own bat, explaining why he was pictured with Collins' equipment instead. The back of Mantle's uniform provides another clue. The visible number is a 6 rather than the No. 7 that became permanently associated with him. Heritage notes that Mantle wore No. 6 only during the unsettled beginning of his rookie campaign before switching to No. 7.The image became the basis for Mantle's rookie cardThe photograph is particularly significant because it became the source for Mantle's 1951 Bowman rookie card. Heritage describes the image as one of the most recognisable photographs of Mantle, although the baseball card altered some of its visual details. The 1951 Bowman version has a distinctive posterised appearance, while Mantle's 1953 Topps card used the same photograph but cropped more tightly around his youthful face. The same image was also used for Mantle's 1952 Berk Ross card. Heritage's records for a separate Type 1 example from the Jack Kramer Collection identify the photograph as the source for the 1951 Bowman and 1953 Topps cards and show Mantle wearing No. 6 with Collins' bat over his shoulder. The garage-sale photograph was classified as Type 2 by PSA/DNA. That distinction matters because it was not one of the rare first-generation prints. Heritage's 2024 records describe the much rarer Type 1 version as an original photograph made from the original negative during the period close to when the picture was taken. PSA's Type 1 classification is based on that first-generation status.The photograph's reverse carried a matching inscriptionThe photograph found in the garage-sale book had handwritten words identifying the subject as "Mickey Mantle" on its reverse. Heritage said the handwriting perfectly matched the handwriting on a Type 1 example of the same photograph that it had sold for $71,700 in 2015. The auction house also noted that it had since sold another Type 1 example for more than $800,000.The $20,740 photograph was not in perfect condition. Heritage noted surface wear on the front, numerous light horizontal cracks in the glossy finish, several small areas of paper loss along the white border and a slight tear on the middle-right side. It had no other markings or stamps and was encapsulated by PSA/DNA as a Type 2 photograph. Despite those imperfections, the photograph retained a direct connection to one of the most recognisable images from Mantle's early career. The combination of its provenance, its use as the source for the 1951 Bowman rookie card and its unusual garage-sale discovery helped make it a notable auction find.A different Type 1 Mantle photograph sold for $843,750The huge difference in value between different generations of the image can be seen in another Heritage sale. On April 7, 2024, the auction house sold a Type 1 print of the same Mantle action photograph for $843,750. The photograph came from the collection of Jack Kramer, a former major-league pitcher who had been Mantle's Yankees teammate. It was an original 8-by-10-inch photograph taken by Yankees team photographer Bob Olen and had remained among Kramer's possessions for decades. Heritage said only four known original prints of the image existed, meaning the $843,750 photograph was one of the rare Type 1 examples. The auction house described the sale as a record for a Type 1 sports photograph, surpassing the previous $516,000 record set by a Ty Cobb photograph.The same 2024 auction also included a different Mantle photograph from the Kramer Collection, a 1951 rookie headshot, which sold for $20,625. That was a separate item from the garage-sale photograph that later sold for $20,740. The distinction explains why the two prices, although strikingly similar, should not be confused. The $20,740 sale concerned the Type 2 photograph discovered inside the garage-sale book, while the $20,625 result concerned a separate Kramer Collection headshot. What began as a couple looking through an old baseball book at a local garage sale ultimately uncovered a photograph tied directly to one of Mickey Mantle's most famous baseball-card images. Heritage sold that Type 2 photograph for $20,740 in December 2025.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: AfD tops another German state poll, Merz’s CDU crashes to historic low
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) emerged as the largest party in Sunday's election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, dealing another .
articles.body: Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) emerged as the largest party in Sunday's election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, dealing another setback to Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU).According to preliminary results, AfD won 38.3 percent of the vote, ahead of the Social Democratic Party (SPD) at 35.4 percent, while the CDU secured just 4.9 percent, its worst result in a state election since 1949.According to Reuters, the result marked the AfD's second first-place finish in a German state election this month, after it came close to an outright majority in Saxony-Anhalt on September 6.In Berlin, meanwhile, the Left Party emerged as the largest party with 25.3 percent, followed by the CDU at 19 percent and the AfD at 16.3 percent.Merz described the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania result as "a disaster" but said he would remain in office and continue with his reform agenda. "What needs to be done now requires backbone, steadfastness, and patience," Merz said after the results.The results add to pressure on Merz, whose government has faced criticism over Germany's weak economy, high living costs and proposed pension, tax and healthcare reforms. The CDU's poor performance also comes as the AfD continues to gain ground in national opinion polls, increasing pressure on the governing coalition.The AfD's strongest gains have been in eastern Germany, where concerns over migration, living costs and Germany's support for Ukraine have featured prominently in political campaigns.Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania's SPD premier Manuela Schwesig said opposition to Berlin's Ukraine policy was among the issues influencing voters."Many people oppose support for Ukraine, both financial and military," Schwesig told Reuters. She added that some voters also wanted Russian energy supplies through the Nord Stream pipelines to resume.Despite its growing electoral support, the AfD remains excluded from government because Germany's major mainstream parties have maintained a political "firewall" against forming coalitions with it. The latest results, however, underline the growing challenge the party poses to Germany's established political parties.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Putin-backed United Russia leads Duma polls with 57.5% as Ukraine war overshadows votes
articles.summary: Europe News: Russia's ruling United Russia party, which supports President Vladimir Putin, has taken a strong early lead in the country's State Duma elections, sec.
articles.body: Russia's ruling United Russia party, which supports President Vladimir Putin, has taken a strong early lead in the country's State Duma elections, securing 57.5 per cent of the vote in initial results.The three-day parliamentary election ended on Sunday, with the final results expected by September 25, according to CNN. Early figures released by Russia's Central Election Commission showed United Russia well ahead of other parties.The election is the first parliamentary vote since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Putin has sought to present the poll as a measure of public support for his government's domestic and military policies.Putin links vote to support for troopsAhead of the election, Putin urged Russians to turn out and portrayed the poll as a show of unity behind the country's military campaign.“Your choice and determination will show once again that millions of people are backing our fighters and that we stand together, united by shared values, our historical memory, love for our Motherland,” Putin said, according to CNN.Putin himself was not a candidate in the election. He is due to face voters in the next presidential election in 2030.United Russia won 324 of the 450 seats in the State Duma in the previous parliamentary election in 2021.Opposition largely absentThe election took place in a tightly controlled political environment, with CNN reporting that meaningful opposition to the Kremlin was largely absent.Yabloko, the country's only registered anti-war party, was prevented from contesting the federal party-list election after Russia's Supreme Court barred it last month.Overall voter turnout stood at 56.66 per cent, according to the Central Election Commission, while participation in Moscow was also reported to be high. With the result largely expected amid the lack of credible opposition, turnout and the final distribution of the 450 seats are being closely watched.Ukraine war overshadows votingThe parliamentary election coincided with intensified military activity between Russia and Ukraine.CNN reported that Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones towards Moscow and the surrounding region on Sunday. Russian officials said at least two people were killed and a major oil refinery was damaged.Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said the attacks were intended to disrupt the election. Ukraine has not independently confirmed that claim.The Kremlin is expected to use the election result to demonstrate domestic support for Putin and his policies, including the war in Ukraine.Russian citizens living abroad also took part in the three-day vote. In India, Russian Ambassador Denis Alipov cast his ballot in New Delhi. Five polling stations were established for Russian citizens across India, including in Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai and Goa.The final results are expected to be announced by September 25, when the composition of the next State Duma will become clear.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A 5-foot venomous snake fell into a chemical-filled industrial tank in Gujarat; after being found unconscious, it was revived with nearly 2 minutes of CPR
articles.summary: Animals & Pets News: A five-foot-long snake was revived after it was found unconscious inside a tank containing chemical-filled water at an industrial unit in Gujarat’s Va.
articles.body: A five-foot-long snake was revived after it was found unconscious inside a tank containing chemical-filled water at an industrial unit in Gujarat’s Vapi. An animal rescuer reportedly performed artificial respiration on the reptile for nearly two minutes before it began showing signs of recovery.The incident took place on Friday at an effluent treatment plant (ETP) at India Gelatine Company Limited (IGCL) in the first phase of Vapi GIDC in Valsad district.According to local reports, the snake had entered the industrial premises and accidentally fallen into a tank containing chemically contaminated water. It was found unconscious after apparently coming into contact with and ingesting the water.Company officials then contacted animal welfare volunteer and snake rescuer Sanjay Pawar.Snake found unconscious in chemical waterPawar reached the spot and removed the snake from the tank. The reptile was reportedly unresponsive at the time. He then began efforts to revive it, administering artificial respiration for nearly two minutes.After initially showing no response, the snake gradually began to move and eventually regained consciousness, according to reports.The rescue was captured on video, which later circulated on social media. The footage shows Pawar attempting to revive the snake after removing it from the chemical-filled tank.Following its recovery, the reptile was taken away from the industrial premises. Reports said it was subsequently released in a forested area after being kept under observation.The rescue also exposed Pawar to the contaminated water. According to local reports, he was kept under medical observation for around 24 hours as a precaution.There are differing descriptions of the snake in local reports. Some have identified it as a Dhaman, or rat snake, and described it as non-venomous, while other reports have referred to it as a venomous snake.Two cobras rescued on the same dayPawar and his team also rescued two cobras from different locations in Vapi on the same day.One cobra was reportedly found at an open plot near Chalna Bhathala Party Plot, while another was rescued from a company premises in the Daman Ganga Industrial Park.The incidents come amid frequent encounters between snakes and human settlements or industrial premises in areas where open plots, factories and surrounding habitats are located close to one another.The unusual rescue in Vapi has drawn attention because of the effort to revive the snake after it was found unconscious. The video shows Pawar continuing the artificial respiration until the reptile began responding.Wildlife rescuers advise people not to attempt to catch or handle snakes themselves, particularly when the species is unknown. In such situations, trained snake rescuers or local wildlife authorities should be contacted.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: US, China launch 'AI dialogue' ahead of Trump-Xi summit amid race to control AI risks
articles.summary: US News: The United States and China have agreed to establish a formal dialogue on artificial intelligence, adding a new area of cooperation between the world'.
articles.body: The United States and China have agreed to establish a formal dialogue on artificial intelligence, adding a new area of cooperation between the world's two biggest AI powers ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Washington.US treasury secretary Scott Bessent announced the agreement after talks with Chinese vice-premier He Lifeng in New York on Sunday. The two sides also moved ahead with plans for a trade mechanism first discussed when Trump met Xi in Beijing.The agreement comes as technology leaders warn that rapid advances in AI could create serious risks if research continues without adequate safeguards.US and China set up AI mechanismUS Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Washington and Beijing had formalised a "board of trade" that had been discussed during Trump's May meeting with Xi in Beijing."We just had a very successful engagement with the Chinese on trade and AI, completing where we left off in Beijing," Bessent said at JPMorgan's headquarters in New York, where the two delegations held talks before the summit."[In Beijing] we created the board of trade and began the subject of AI, and this evening those were operationalised," Bessent was quoted as saying by FT.Washington has also proposed a "notification mechanism" to address AI-related incidents involving national security. Bessent said the new dialogue could help the two countries develop "a shared vision of common goals and common threats"."We think that just like any cross-border activity that is moving from opaque to more transparency between the number one and number two AI powers in the world is very important," he added.Trade truce and rare earths remain keyThe talks also focused on whether Washington and Beijing can extend the one-year trade truce agreed by Trump and Xi in Busan, South Korea, last October.The agreement had temporarily eased tensions in their trade war. The US agreed to delay export controls that could have affected thousands of Chinese companies, while China agreed to postpone sweeping restrictions on rare earth exports.China has sought to extend the truce until the end of Trump's second term, according to people familiar with the discussions. The US, however, has been pushing for a shorter extension of about six months.Washington has raised concerns that Beijing has not fully implemented commitments on rare earths. US companies have faced delays in obtaining the materials, which are important for several industries and supply chains. The US has also raised concerns about Chinese restrictions affecting rare earth exports to Japan.Trump and Xi set for Washington summitAI, Taiwan, Iran and the future of the trade truce are among the issues expected to feature in the Trump-Xi meeting.Trump is due to welcome Xi at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday before the leaders hold their summit on Thursday, which will include a state dinner for the Chinese president.The meeting comes four months after Xi hosted Trump for a state visit in Beijing. It will also be their first meeting on US soil since Trump's first term, when they met at Mar-a-Lago in 2017.Bessent and Greer have held several rounds of talks with He since the US-China trade war began in early 2025. The New York discussions were their first meeting outside Europe and Asia.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Four sisters started a Thai-inspired popcorn brand after a family trip; it now makes $7,000 a month
articles.summary: US News: The Lertlumprasert sisters, Lisa, Lita, Charlene and Charlie, had talked about starting a business together since childhood. That idea finally took sh.
articles.body: The Lertlumprasert sisters, Lisa, Lita, Charlene and Charlie, had talked about starting a business together since childhood. That idea finally took shape in February 2023, after a family trip to Thailand left them with a suitcase full of snacks their American friends loved. Combined with their frustration over the "better-for-you" snack options available in the US, the trip inspired their Thai-inspired popcorn brand, Party Of. Here's how the Washington, DC-based sisters built the business from a homemade batch into a side hustle generating steady monthly revenue.How a trip to Thailand inspired the Lertlumprasert sisters' popcorn brandAccording to Lita, a data scientist, the sisters had returned from visiting family in Thailand with an abundance of Thai snacks to share with friends, who loved everything they brought back. As reported by Entrepreneur, what experience, paired with the sisters' shared sense that healthier snack options in the US weren't inspiring, led them to take classic, accessible snack foods and give them their own signature spin. Lisa, who owns and operates Thai restaurants, brought culinary experience to the idea, while Lita's data science background, Charlene's UX design skills and Charlie's product management expertise rounded out the founding team behind what would become Party Of.Launching Party Of: branding investment and early recipe developmentTo get the business off the ground, the sisters began by defining what Charlie, a product manager, called the six dimensions of product-market fit, target customer, problem, value proposition, competitive advantage, growth strategy and business model. Identifying branding as a key competitive advantage, they invested $28,000 to work with branding agency Outline. Recipe development and inventory costs stayed low early on, since Lisa used ingredients already available at her restaurant, bought corn and brown bags, and applied a "ZingPop" sticker, later rebranded Party Of, that Charlene designed on Canva. The StartupCPG Slack group later became an invaluable free resource for learning and connecting with other CPG entrepreneurs.A production crisis during Compass Group's Retail Incubator ProgramThe sisters' biggest challenge came during their participation in Compass Group's Retail Incubator Program, which required them to produce over 30,000 units in under four months, more than they had sold in total during the seven months since launching. To hit that number, the team had to switch to a new pillow-pouch format entirely, which meant reworking the packaging design, getting up to speed on material compositions, and bringing on a different co-packer once their existing setup couldn't handle the equipment or scale required. Things didn't go smoothly from there either, bags weren't cutting cleanly on the production line, shipments got stuck at customs, and tariffs added another unexpected hit. The sisters got through it the way they'd gotten through everything else so far, calling on people in their network and trusting their best judgment even without all the answers.Party Of's growth and the sisters' advice for other foundersBy 2025, Party Of's revenue had grown fourfold from the year before, and the sisters trimmed their cost of goods sold by roughly a quarter, numbers Lisa points to as proof the harder years of building the brand are starting to pay off. Monthly revenue now sits at a fairly steady $7,000, though every so often a bigger order comes through, anywhere from $5,000 to $50,000, on top of that baseline. For Charlene, the payoff isn't just financial; having full say over every decision is a kind of satisfaction she never got from a corporate role. Lisa's advice to anyone starting echoes how they began, nail down product-market fit before anything else, because that early clarity spares you from wasted effort later. Charlene's one regret, if she's honest, is not treating the books seriously sooner.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Australian couple spent $500,000 building their retirement home; it was constructed on the wrong block and later had to be moved 100 metres
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Melanie and David Moor spent more than $500,000 on what they expected to be their retirement home in Camperdown, south-west Victoria, only to discover.
articles.body: Melanie and David Moor spent more than $500,000 on what they expected to be their retirement home in Camperdown, south-west Victoria, only to discover that the house had been placed entirely on a neighbouring block. The couple had bought land in a new subdivision in 2021 and, after obtaining permits, installed a driveway and relocated a four-bedroom house onto the 2-hectare property they believed they owned. Instead, the house had been moved onto the adjacent block, which belonged to someone else. The mistake was discovered in August 2024, while the Moors were completing work on the house, after a council officer told David Moor to stop construction and seek legal advice. The couple then spent almost two years trying to resolve the dispute, including an unsuccessful proposal to swap the two properties. In April 2026, the house was finally moved about 100 metres onto the block the Moors actually owned.The confusion began when the land was still an undivided paddockThe Moors first viewed the subdivision in August 2021, when the land was still part of a larger 8-hectare paddock that had not yet been divided into individual lots. They paid a $5,000 deposit and signed the contract of sale in April 2022. Melanie Moor told ABC that the couple believed they had identified the correct block after a real estate agent showed them the property, while numbers on nearby fence posts also contributed to their understanding of which lot they had purchased.The real estate agency later said an internal investigation found that its agent had not made false or misleading claims. A spokesperson said the agent had shown the couple the property well before the contract was signed and while it was still part of the larger paddock, adding that it was ultimately the buyers' responsibility to confirm which block they owned. The confusion continued after the purchase. In 2023, before settlement, the Moors had a driveway constructed on the block they believed was theirs, with permission from the former owner of the neighbouring property. When the house was later relocated, the builder and other tradespeople used that driveway as a reference point for identifying the lot. ABC reported that the relocation company's job document listed the road name but not a specific lot number.Council inspections did not catch the mistakeThe Moors obtained a building permit from Corangamite Shire Council in April 2024. However, documents supporting the permit included an aerial photograph showing that soil samples had been taken from the wrong block. Council records also showed that staff visited the site three times in one month to inspect stump holes dug for the house relocation.The mistake was finally identified in August 2024, while the Moors were putting the finishing touches on the house. A council officer contacted David Moor, instructed him to stop work and advised him to seek legal advice. Melanie said the couple initially thought the call was a scam before realising that their new home was sitting entirely on land they did not own. The actual owner of that block lived interstate and had purchased the property from their late uncle. According to the owner's lawyers, the owner had been unaware that the Moors had moved a house onto the land until after the work had taken place.A proposed land swap failed over differences between the blocksOnce the mistake was discovered, the Moors proposed swapping the block where their house had been placed with the neighbouring block they actually owned. The proposal was rejected by the other landowner's lawyers, who said the properties were not equivalent. They pointed to differences in the views from each block, a registered easement on the Moors' property and possible tax consequences from a land swap.The dispute eventually became a legal matter. In July 2025, the landowner's lawyers gave the Moors 14 days to remove the house and restore the property to its original condition, warning that the house could otherwise be sold. At the time, the Moors said they could not afford to move it. The contractor who had originally relocated the house also advised that it might not survive another move. The situation was particularly difficult because Victoria's property laws do not give courts the same range of options available in some other Australian jurisdictions for cases in which someone mistakenly builds on another person's land. An ABC report examining the issue noted that such cases are sometimes referred to as the "mistaken improver" problem.The house was moved 100 metres onto the correct blockAfter months of negotiations, the parties reached an agreement in February 2026 for the Moors to clear the disputed property by May 2. The couple eventually found another house mover who was willing to take on the job after their original contractor had warned against a second relocation. Just before Easter, the four-bedroom house was lifted and transported about 100 metres sideways onto the Moors' actual property. The couple described seeing the house transferred onto their own land as a major relief after the prolonged dispute.The move has not yet made the house habitable. The building is temporarily sitting on empty oil drums while it waits to be restumped. Its septic system and electrical wiring had to be disconnected and removed during the relocation, and the Moors said they do not yet know how much structural damage the house may have suffered. Melanie said the house appeared unstable during the move and that the family was not yet comfortable entering it.The couple also have to restore the neighbouring property. They said they need to remove about 160 stumps left where the house had stood and take out trees they had planted before returning the block to its original condition. They estimate the relocation, restumping and reconnection of electricity and other services will cost about $100,000, on top of the more than $500,000 already spent on the home. For now, the Moors have bought a 20-foot caravan and plan to live there with their 20-year-old daughter while they work to make the house liveable. Melanie said the ordeal had taken a significant toll on the family's mental health, but the couple remained determined to finish their retirement home.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang rejects Dario Amodei and Sam Altman’s 'AI will kill us all warnings': ‘Don't let this doomsday narrative cause somebody to…’
articles.summary: Tech News News: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has outrightly rejected the apocalyptic claims that artificial intelligence (AI) will cause the extinction of humanity in the .
articles.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has outrightly rejected the apocalyptic claims that artificial intelligence (AI) will cause the extinction of humanity in the coming years, dismissing such warnings as baseless and exaggerated scare tactics. Speaking with CBS News, Huang challenged these ‘doomsday predictions’ voiced by prominent tech leaders, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI’s Sam Altman, cautioning the public and lawmakers not to be misled by panic.“Don't let this doomsday narrative cause somebody to relieve them of the laws that currently exist," Huang stated in an interview, adding, “Read between the lines. They're actually not asking for more laws. They're asking to be relieved of the laws we do have. And I think that that's a problem. We have plenty of laws, so let's apply those first.”Jensen Huang says ‘no’ to 2030 extinction threatHuang’s comments follow a heated public dispute triggered earlier this month by Jacob Coxon, a former researcher at Anthropic. Coxon posted on social media that developers of frontier AI models believe the technology could wipe out humanity before the decade concludes.This ignited widespread controversy and prompted Amodei, Altman and Elon Musk to urge a deliberate slow down in model development. Huang flatly rejected those forecasts, arguing they have no grounding in scientific reality.“2030 is not going to be the end of the world. There is 0% chance that's going to be the end of the world. Scaring people is unnecessary. It is irresponsible,” Huang added.As the biggest producer of specialised chips powering AI models developed by OpenAI and competing labs, Nvidia holds an immense financial stake in the conversation. Soaring demand for its graphics processors has driven the company's valuation to $5.3 trillion, solidifying its rank as the world's most valuable enterprise.When asked why the public should accept his safety assurances given Nvidia’s obvious financial motives, Huang maintained that corporate health depends entirely on dependable technology.“Our company's success is directly connected to the safe deployment of products and services. If we don't continue to do that, our value would be diminished,” he noted.Huang also said that current American frameworks dealing with unauthorised computer access, damage liabilities and product safety are more than adequate.Get the latest technology news and updates.
